newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan not mulling new public funds to buy land-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan not mulling new public funds to buy land-MOF.

text.p: The Japanese government is not considering allocating new public funds to buy collateralised land formerly owned by troubled financial firms to promote liquidity of land transactions, a Finance Ministry official told Reuters on Thursday.

But the official said using public funds to purchase land for public parks with money already set aside in the state budget for the year starting on April 1 was being considered as one of numerous measures to promote land liquidity.
Such parks could also be used as neighbourhood assembly points during disasters such as major earthquakes, she said.
The official said the panel hopes to finalise proposals for promotion of land transactions by the end of March.

A front-page report in Thursday's edition of business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that the government plans to use more public funds to buy collateralised land previously owned by failed "jusen" mortgage firms and other troubled financial firms helped push up Tokyo share prices on Thursday morning.
"We are very surprised by the fact that the stock market was so overjoyed at the news," the official said.
The government is studying securitisation of land as one of the main measures to promote land liquidity, she added.
Real estate values in Japan have plummeted since the bursting in the early 1990s of an economic "bubble" of inflated asset prices.
The government panel was established last October to tackle the tough issue of collecting problem loans for which land is being held as collateral.

The panel, whose members include officials from the Finance, Construction and Justice ministries and the National Land Agency, is discussing how to increase liquidity in the property market to facilitate collection of problem loans.
